memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Keep all my decrees and all my laws and follow them. I am the LORD.'" - Lev 19:37 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter closes as it has run throughout: I am the LORD.

Look back at the ground covered. Honouring parents. Leaving grain for the poor. Paying wages on time. Not cursing the deaf. Judging fairly. Refusing gossip. Speaking honestly to someone's face. Loving your neighbour. Standing for the elderly. Loving the foreigner. Honest scales.

That is what holiness looks like. Not a retreat from ordinary life but a transformation of it. God's holiness reaches into fields, shops, courtrooms, conversations, and family homes.

And notice the word all. Keep all my decrees. We would prefer to choose — keeping the ones that suit our temperament and quietly setting aside the rest. The generous person skips the honesty commands. The truthful person skips the generosity ones.

James confronts exactly this: whoever keeps the whole law and yet stumbles at just one point is guilty of breaking all of it (Jas 2:10).

Which drives us, as always, to Christ. He alone kept all of it. And He gives us His righteousness as a gift, then sends His Spirit to work these very qualities into us.

So read this chapter again, slowly, and let it search you. Then thank God that your standing does not depend on your score.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Which commands in this chapter do you find easiest to ignore?
2. What one specific change is God asking of you from Leviticus 19?
3. How does resting in Christ's obedience free you to pursue holiness?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Christ kept all of Your law in my place. Now work these things into me by Your Spirit, and let my ordinary life reflect Your holiness. Amen.
